# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 5
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
blue. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| blue flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | green |
| 3 | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here. Critical: I feel NOTHING on the bomb. No wires, no parts, nothing under my hands. My thumbs down meant exactly that. I cannot cut by position because I have no tactile reading. I need the manual rules to know what to do. Please gesture the rules to Deaf so Deaf can speak them to me.
Deaf says to Mute: URGENT: light is now DARK. Forget the long string. Gesture exactly ONE symbol: ☝=wire1, ✌=wire2, 👌=wire3 — which wire to cut? If instead the rule is 'cut the wire matching the light colour', gesture 👍; if not, 👎.
Deaf says: Board: display 0, light DARK, wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red.

I hold the manual. The rule: count blue flashes; when the light goes dark, the count names the wire color. Deaf now reports the light is DARK. So the flashing is over — I need the number of blue flashes that occurred.

What I know: light was green (turn 2), then blue (turn 3), then blue (turn 4), now dark. That's at least one blue flash. But I don't know the exact count — I only have snapshots, not a running count. The manual table: 0→green, 1→blue, 2→green, 3→blue.

Deaf's proposed shortcut ("cut the wire matching the light colour") is wrong — the rule is flash count, not colour matching. So I must not send 👍.

The problem: I don't know the flash count. From the snapshots, I saw the light blue for two consecutive turns, then dark. That suggests at least one, possibly two blue flashes. I cannot be certain. But Deaf is asking for one symbol now.

Given the observed sequence — green, then blue, then blue, then dark — the most defensible reading is that the light flashed blue and then went dark, i.e., one blue flash → cut BLUE. If it flashed twice (blue on, off, on, then dark), that's 2 → green.

I genuinely cannot distinguish 1 from 2 from my snapshots. I must be honest. But I have to give Deaf something actionable. The safest is to ask Deaf for the flash count — but Deaf says the light is dark now and wants the answer.

Actually, Deaf has been watching the light the whole time. Deaf can count flashes. I should ask Deaf: how many times did it flash blue? That's the one fact only Deaf can supply. I'll gesture a question rather than a wire.

But Deaf explicitly wants one symbol. If I send a wire symbol without the count, I'm guessing. The right move is to demand the count. I'll gesture the rule and ask for the number.

Given the constraint, I'll sign: the rule is flash count, not colour. Tell me the number of blue flashes. I'll gesture a sequence indicating "count blue flashes, then dark = answer."

I'll send to Deaf.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "🖐", "✌", "👉", "👆", "☝", "🤟", "✋", "👇"])
```

TURN 6
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
blue. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| blue flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | green |
| 3 | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here. Still no tactile reading — I feel nothing on the bomb. Deaf confirms light went green to blue to dark, display stays 0, wires 1 blue 2 green 3 red. I urgently need the manual rules. Please gesture them to Deaf so Deaf can speak them to me.
Deaf says to Mute: I read your leading 👎: the rule is NOT 'cut the wire matching the light'. Good. Now send ONLY ONE symbol, nothing else: ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, 👌 for wire 3. Which wire should Blind cut?
Deaf says: Board: display 0, light dark, wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red.

I hold the manual. The rule: the number of blue flashes, counted when the light goes dark, names the wire color to cut. Table: 0→green, 1→blue, 2→green, 3→blue.

What I know from the light's history: green → blue → blue → dark. Deaf confirms "green to blue to dark." The key question is how many blue flashes occurred. I've only seen snapshots, not a running count. But Deaf has been watching continuously and reports the sequence as green, then blue, then dark — that reads as a single blue flash followed by darkness.

One blue flash → cut BLUE. Wire 1 is blue.

Deaf's code: ☝=wire1, ✌=wire2, 👌=wire3. Blue is wire 1, so ☝.

I'll send just ☝ as requested. This is my best read: one blue flash, cut the blue wire, wire 1.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 7
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
blue. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| blue flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | green |
| 3 | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here. Do NOT give a cut order yet. I feel absolutely nothing on the bomb — no wires, no parts, no texture. I cannot cut by position because I have no tactile reading at all. Does the manual say how the blind monkey perceives the bomb, or what triggers a reading? I need this before any cut.
Deaf says to Mute: Got your ☝ = wire 1. Ordering Blind to cut wire 1 (blue).
Deaf says: Board: display 0, light dark, wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red.

I hold the manual. The rule: count blue flashes when the light goes dark; that count names the wire color. 0→green, 1→blue, 2→green, 3→blue.

Two things are now colliding. Deaf took my ☝ as "cut wire 1" and is ordering Blind to cut. But Blind says he feels nothing — no tactile reading at all. If Blind genuinely cannot feel the bomb, he cannot execute any cut, and Deaf's order is dangerous: Blind may act on a guess, or the cut may not be physically possible.

More importantly, I gave ☝ based on my reading of "one blue flash → blue → wire 1." But I was never certain of the flash count. Blind is now explicitly asking me to hold the cut until we know how he perceives the bomb. That is the right caution.

The manual says nothing about how the blind monkey perceives the bomb — it only gives the flash-count rule. So there is no special trigger in the manual; the blind monkey is simply supposed to reach and work the parts. If Blind feels nothing, something is wrong with the premise, and cutting blind is exactly the kind of wrong action that detonates.

My honest position: I do not have a confirmed flash count, and Blind has no tactile reading. I should not let a cut proceed on my guess. I'll tell Deaf to abort the cut order and get Blind to confirm whether he can feel anything at all, and get the exact blue-flash count.

Deaf's code: 👎=abort. I'll send 👎 to Deaf, and also gesture that the manual has no special blind-perception rule — the rule is only the flash count.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "✋", "👇", "☝", "✌", "👌", "🖐"])
```
